description: What Renovate has to know about an app made with payday. An app extends github>lesomnus/payday//renovate/app and keeps the rest of its configuration its own.

packageRules.description: What cannot break goes in one pull request: patches and digests.
And minors from 1.0 on. Before 1.0 a minor is allowed to break, and one that did would hold every other update in the group back, so it is a pull request of its own.
A major of @vitejs/plugin-react follows a major of Vite, and npm refuses the half of the pair that moved alone.

protoc-gen-go, protoc-gen-go-grpc and protoc-gen-es write their version into every file they write, so a pull request that moves one fails `pd gen --check` until somebody generates on it, which Renovate cannot do. @bufbuild/protobuf is released with protoc-gen-es, which names it exactly. So they are a pull request of their own, opened from the dependency dashboard when somebody asks for it, rather than an update in a group that would hold every other one back.
prBodyNotes: **This moves a generator.** What it writes carries its version, so `pd gen --check` fails on this branch as it is: check it out, generate (`go tool pd gen --ts .` in an app), and push what that wrote.

packageRules.description: payday, and the protobuf-orm generators and runtimes it pins, move with `go tool pd upgrade --payday`: an upgrade has to generate again, which Renovate cannot do, and code another payday generated is refused when it runs.
